postcards.title: Margin Note Market Button Stand
postcards.useCase: Upper-age printable postcard for thanking someone for a small object, helpful errand, or shared supplies after a homeschool table activity.
postcards.adultSetup: Print the card, offer a pencil, and ask the child to pick one safe ordinary object from the table as the invented market detail.
postcards.kidDirection: Write a sincere thank-you note that names one real helpful thing, then adds a tiny invented margin-market detail to make the note warm.
postcards.noteStarter: Start with a direct thank-you and one specific detail about what helped you: __________.
postcards.storyBridge: Turn the helpful thing into a tiny market stall clue, such as a button basket, folded receipt, or pencil label: __________.
postcards.politeClose: Close with one kind sentence that says why the gesture mattered today: __________.
postcards.drawingPrompt: Draw a margin-note market stall with one ordinary object label: __________.
postcards.revisionNudge: Revise by replacing a general word like nice or good with a more exact gratitude word: __________.
postcards.quietOption: Quiet option: skip the story scene and write only one clear thank-you detail: __________.
postcards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: A sincere note gets stronger when one real thank-you detail meets one tiny invented clue: __________.

postcards.title: Index Card Theater Prop Thanks
postcards.useCase: Printable postcard for a child thanking a helper, tutor, relative, or family friend after receiving time, help, or a simple item.
postcards.adultSetup: Print the postcard and set out two blank index cards so the child can imagine a tiny stage without performing or sharing aloud.
postcards.kidDirection: Write a note with two short kind sentences, then invent one stage prop that quietly shows the thank-you feeling.
postcards.noteStarter: Begin with a thank-you sentence that sounds like your own voice: __________.
postcards.storyBridge: Add a tiny theater prop, curtain tag, or stage cue that connects to the thank-you: __________.
postcards.politeClose: Close with a kind sentence that does not ask for anything back: __________.
postcards.drawingPrompt: Draw two index cards on a tiny stage, with one prop labeled: __________.
postcards.revisionNudge: Revise one sentence so it sounds warmer and less rushed: __________.
postcards.quietOption: Quiet option: write the note as two quiet stage lines and one close: __________.
postcards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: A kind thank-you note can be short, clear, and still feel personal: __________.

postcards.title: Revision River Ferry Gift Bridge
postcards.useCase: Upper-age printable postcard for turning a thank-you about a simple gift, borrowed supply, or thoughtful help into a short story detail.
postcards.adultSetup: Print the postcard, remind the child to focus on thanks rather than size or value, and invite them to choose one pretend ferry cargo detail.
postcards.kidDirection: Name the real thank-you reason, then build a small ferry image that carries the object or helpful moment into a story.
postcards.noteStarter: Start by thanking the person for the gift, help, or time with one exact detail: __________.
postcards.storyBridge: Imagine the thanked-for thing riding across Revision River as safe ferry cargo: __________.
postcards.politeClose: Close by saying how you will use, remember, or appreciate the gesture: __________.
postcards.drawingPrompt: Draw a little ferry carrying one ordinary object with a thank-you tag: __________.
postcards.revisionNudge: Revise the bridge sentence so the real thanks and invented ferry detail connect clearly: __________.
postcards.quietOption: Quiet option: write one real thank-you sentence and one ferry cargo phrase: __________.
postcards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: The best bridge sentence keeps the gratitude real and the story detail tiny: __________.

postcards.title: Clue Label Tower Memory Exhibit
postcards.useCase: Printable postcard for thanking someone after a visit, lesson, ride, meal, or shared activity by naming one remembered ordinary detail.
postcards.adultSetup: Print the card and invite the child to pick one ordinary remembered object, sound, color, or moment from the day.
postcards.kidDirection: Write a thank-you note that labels one remembered detail like a museum clue, then explains why it made the moment better.
postcards.noteStarter: Start with thanks for the visit, lesson, ride, meal, or shared time: __________.
postcards.storyBridge: Make one remembered detail into a pretend museum clue label: __________.
postcards.politeClose: Close with one sentence about why that memory will be easy to keep: __________.
postcards.drawingPrompt: Draw a tower museum label for one ordinary memory object: __________.
postcards.revisionNudge: Revise by adding one exact memory detail instead of a broad phrase: __________.
postcards.quietOption: Quiet option: list one memory clue first, then turn it into a sentence: __________.
postcards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: One exact memory detail can make a thank-you note feel sincere: __________.

postcards.title: Binding Day Boardwalk Polished Postcard
postcards.useCase: Upper-age printable postcard for revising a thank-you draft before handing it to a family member, tutor, neighbor, or helper.
postcards.adultSetup: Print the postcard and give the child a scrap paper draft space so the final postcard can stay neat and low-pressure.
postcards.kidDirection: Draft a quick thank-you, then use one binding-day boardwalk detail to polish the note before copying the final version.
postcards.noteStarter: Draft the first thank-you sentence before polishing it: __________.
postcards.storyBridge: Add a boardwalk ticket, folded page, or paper string detail that matches the gratitude: __________.
postcards.politeClose: Close with a polished sentence that feels finished but not fancy: __________.
postcards.drawingPrompt: Draw a boardwalk postcard stand with one tied-up thank-you page: __________.
postcards.revisionNudge: Revise by checking for one clear detail, one kind sentence, and one tidy close: __________.
postcards.quietOption: Quiet option: polish only one sentence and copy it carefully here: __________.
postcards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: A polished thank-you note is specific, kind, and easy to read: __________.

postcards.title: Compass Craft Academy Thanks Route
postcards.useCase: Printable postcard for helping kids plan a clear beginning, middle, and close for a sincere thank-you note.
postcards.adultSetup: Print the postcard and invite the child to mark three compass points: what happened, why it mattered, and the closing thanks.
postcards.kidDirection: Map the thank-you note like a three-stop route, then add one invented compass-craft detail without asking for a reply.
postcards.noteStarter: Start at the first compass point by naming what you are thankful for: __________.
postcards.storyBridge: Move to the second point with a tiny map, compass, or craft-room detail: __________.
postcards.politeClose: End at the final point with a polite close that asks for nothing: __________.
postcards.drawingPrompt: Draw a three-stop compass route for the thank-you note: __________.
postcards.revisionNudge: Revise the route so the note moves from thanks to detail to close in order: __________.
postcards.quietOption: Quiet option: fill only the three route points before writing the final note: __________.
postcards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: A clear thank-you route helps the reader feel the real gratitude: __________.
